To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there was no statistically significant acceleration in MDG indicators after the 2000 MDGs Declaration, 2) the MDG indicators that did experience a significant acceleration did so before the MDGs declaration, 3) there is no statistically significant evidence of an impact of MDGs-related activities on MDG indicators, and 4) the MDGs did not provide an overall acceleration in development progress in the developing world. [from abstract] Causal Inference, MDGs, Millennium

the MDG indicators experienced a statistically significant acceleration for only one of the eight MDG indicators (Debt Service) and this was for the entire group of developing countries and not just for the IDA-only countries.

the MDGs were not responsible for an acceleration in the MDG development indicators and that the MDGs may have sustained accelerations that had occurred in some MDG indicators before 2000 and may have helped ward off deceleration in some MDG development indicators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the broader issue of the impact of the Millennium Development Goals and not the impact of ODA.
the broader question of whether the activities associated with the Millennium Declaration and the Millennium Development Goal process had an impact on development indicators.
the broader question of whether the MDGs accelerated development in the developing world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MDGs provided an acceleration in progress for only one of the eight indicators and that the MDGs did not provide an overall acceleration in the other seven.
the MDGs were not associated with an acceleration in progress in the MDG Indicators.
, based on the data, the MDGs did not accelerate development outcomes in the developing world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MDGs did not accelerate progress in most of the MDG development indicators and that the MDGs should not be viewed as the primary cause for progress that occurred in the development indicators.
the data does not show that the activities following 2000 accelerated progress in most MDGs.

while the MDGs were a useful tool to focus global attention on development issues, they did not provide a statistically significant acceleration to the development indicators that they were designed to address.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MDG Declaration and the subsequent MDG activities did not provide a global acceleration in development progress.
the MDG-related development activities did not result in an acceleration for the majority of the MDGs and that the MDGs did not provide a global acceleration in development progress.
the MDGs did not provide a global acceleration in the development indicators that were selected for the MDGs.
